learning_outcomes.text: Application of the acquired basic knowledge using the example of a refrigeration system.

Independent recognition of relationships, initiated by understanding executed refrigeration systems. The occurring machine-technical problems should be reliably identified, described, evaluated, and solved. From this, scientifically sound judgments about the mode of operation are to be derived, demonstrated in further new applications, and interface problems recognized.
Work on tasks in interdisciplinary team collaboration.

syllabus_topics: Thermodynamic principles of the cycle of a refrigeration system
Structure and function of the components of a refrigeration cycle:
Piston compressors (cycle, pV diagram, power, volumetric efficiency, efficiency, ..)
Scroll compressors and other types of compressors
Expansion valve function and various designs
Internal heat exchanger for optimizing a system
Heat exchanger evaporators and condensers; various designs of evaporators (flooded evaporators)
Overview of refrigerants (R134a to R744) (normal refrigeration; low-temperature refrigeration; GWP value)
Overview of types of refrigeration systems (e.g., cascade)
Operating behavior and control of a refrigeration system
Regulations for handling refrigerants (F-gas regulation for refrigerants; GWP value)
Use of natural refrigerants such as R290; safety and standards (e.g., EN378); indirect cooling with brine circuit
TEWI method for assessing the environmental compatibility of a refrigeration system
Subcritical and transcritical condensation operation for the refrigerant R744
Design variants of refrigeration systems with R744 (ejector; booster; parallel compressor; etc.)
Heat pumps with natural refrigerants (air and brine); high-temperature heat pump
Combined system for refrigeration and heat pump operation
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module examination.
